tool_calls.result: Adulis was the principal port of the Kingdom of Axum.  - It lay on the Gulf of Zula on the Red Sea, roughly 20‑30 km south of the modern town of Massawa (Eritrea).  - From the 1st century CE until the 7th century CE Adulis served as Axum’s main commercial outlet, facilitating trade between the interior of Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, and the wider Indian Ocean.  - Roman, Egyptian, and later Greek/Byzantine traders frequently recorded Adulis in their accounts, and its harbor was used by Aksumite fleets and merchants carrying ivory, spices, and other goods.  - The port’s prominence persisted until it was largely abandoned in the 7th century CE, when Muslim raids and changing trade routes diminished its role.
